samples.ref: Ama-Atypical Fibrin Fibre Network (izakhi ezingajwayelekile) esifeni samathambo nobudlelwane kokuvuvukaka, i-autoimmunity ne-Thrombosis

```
In-vitro studies have shown that the presence of Atypical Fibrin Fibre Network (AFFN) is associated with increased levels of inflammation and a higher risk of thrombosis in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.  The AFFN is thought to play a role in the pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis by promoting autoimmunity and inflammation.  Furthermore, the presence of AFFN has been linked to a poorer prognosis in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.  The study also investigated the relationship between AFFN and the development of thrombosis in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.  The results showed that the presence of AFFN was significantly associated with an increased risk of thrombosis in these patients.  The study suggests that targeting the AFFN may be a potential therapeutic strategy for managing rheumatoid arthritis and related complications.
```

Izifundo ezithathwe endaweni yangolwazi (in-vitro) zibonise ukuthi khona ukuba khona kwe-Atypical Fibrin Fibre Network (AFFN) kuhambisana nezinga eliphezulu le-inflammation kanye nengozi ephezulu ye-thrombosis kubagulana abanokugula okubizwa nge-isifo samathambo.  Kucatshangwa ukuthi i-AFFN idlala indima ekwelapheni kwe-isifo samathambo ngokukhuthaza ukungatheleleki kanye ne-inflammation.  Ngokwengeziwe, ukuba khona kwe-AFFN kuhambisane nempumela engcono kabi kubagulana abanokugula okubizwa nge-isifo samathambo.  Ucwaningo lwaluhlose ukuhlola ubuhlobo phakathi kwe-AFFN nokwanda kwe-thrombosis kubagulana abanokugula okubizwa nge-isifo samathambo.  Imiphumela ibonise ukuthi ukuba khona kwe-AFFN kuhambisana kakhulu nengozi ephezulu ye-thrombosis kubo abagulana. Female genital cutting/mutilation is a traditional practice that involves the partial or total removal of the external female genitalia or injury to the female genital organs for non-medical purposes.

The practice is often carried out by traditional healers or circumcisers, and is often performed without the informed consent of the woman.

Female genital cutting/mutilation is a violation of human rights, including the right to health, the right to bodily integrity, and the right to freedom from torture and cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment.

Female genital cutting/muling is a public health problem that requires a comprehensive and coordinated response.

The World Health Organization (WHO) is working to eliminate female genital cutting/mutilation worldwide.

The WHO is working with governments, civil society organizations, and communities to raise awareness about the harmful effects of female genital cutting/mutilation and to promote the abandonment of this practice.

The WHO is also supporting research to better understand the causes and consequences of female genital cutting/muling and to develop effective strategies for its prevention.

Le ngxenye yocwaningo ihlose ukutholwa ukuthi ukwanda kwamahlalakhubo egazi elingaphakathi kwabantwana abangaphansi kweminyaka emihlanu endaweni ye-Jimma. Abantwana abangu-384 bahlanganiswe kulo cwaningo, futhi idatha iqoqwe ngokuxoxa nanamadodakazi abo. Imiphumela ibonise ukuthi ukwanda kwamahlalakhubo egazi elingaphakathi kwabantwana abahlanganyelwe kulo cwaningo kwaku-45.6%. Amahlalakhubo avamile atholwe kwaku-Giardia lamblia kanye ne-Entamoeba histolytica.
